Using hydrogen–deuterium exchange mass spectrometry, the team measured conformational changes in the kinase domain upon ligand binding across 38 compounds. Deuterium uptake decreased significantly (p < 0.01) in the activation loop for compounds that stabilized the inactive state, while uptake increased near the hinge region for those that favored an active-like conformation. Clustering the uptake profiles yielded three distinct classes; the third, previously unreported, showed protection in the C-helix without altering the ATP-binding pocket, consistent with an allosteric mechanism. Crystal structures of two representative compounds confirmed a binding site adjacent to the helix. These results suggest that dynamics, and not only static structure, can be used to classify inhibitors and may guide the design of more selective drugs.
